classification.difficultyReason: Identify a suitable parallelogram test from diameters, parallel ruler edges and compass constructions.

children.label: a
children.prompt: In the diagram to the right, both circles have centre $O$. The interval $AOB$ is a diameter of the smaller circle, and $POQ$ is a diameter of the larger circle. What sort of figure is $APBQ$, and why?

spec.description: Concentric circles with solid diameters AB and PQ and a dashed highlighted quadrilateral APBQ.
spec.mathematics: A and B are antipodal on the smaller circle; P and Q are antipodal on the larger circle; both diameters pass through O.
spec.answerVisibility: All givens visible; no answer annotations.

answer.short: $APBQ$ is a parallelogram because its diagonals bisect each other.
answer.worked: $OA=OB$ because they are radii of the smaller circle, and $OP=OQ$ because they are radii of the larger circle. Thus the diagonals $AB$ and $PQ$ bisect each other at $O$. Therefore $APBQ$ is a parallelogram.

children.label: b
children.prompt: The opposite edges of my ruler are parallel. I draw intervals $LM$ and $ST$ of length $4\text{ cm}$ on the opposite edges of the ruler, as shown in the diagram to the right. What sort of figure is $LMST$, and why?

spec.description: Oblique parallel ruler edges with unnumbered graduations and dashed cross-ruler joins LT and MS. Decorative area fill omitted under house diagram policy.
spec.mathematics: L and M lie on one edge; T and S lie on the other in corresponding order. LM and ST are equal by the stated 4 cm givens.
spec.answerVisibility: No additional lengths or conclusions shown.

answer.short: $LMST$ is a parallelogram: $LM$ and $ST$ are equal and parallel opposite sides.
answer.worked: $LM=ST=4\text{ cm}$ (given), and $LM\parallel ST$ because they lie on opposite parallel edges of the ruler. A quadrilateral with one pair of opposite sides equal and parallel is a parallelogram. Therefore $LMST$ is a parallelogram.

children.label: c
children.prompt: In the diagram to the right, $\angle AOB$ is any given angle. First I draw an arc with centre $A$ and radius $OB$. Then I draw an arc with centre $B$ and radius $OA$. The two arcs meet at $M$, and I claim that $AMBO$ is a parallelogram. Am I correct? Explain why or why not.

spec.description: Given angle AOB and intersecting compass arcs at the displayed intersection M; constructed sides AM and MB dashed.
spec.mathematics: The arc centred at A has radius OB; the arc centred at B has radius OA. M is the intersection opposite O across AB.
spec.answerVisibility: Construction only; no equality ticks or conclusion supplied.

answer.short: Yes. $AM=OB$ and $BM=OA$ by construction, so both pairs of opposite sides of $AMBO$ are equal.
answer.worked: $AM=OB$ because the first arc has centre $A$ and radius $OB$. Similarly, $BM=OA$ because the second arc has centre $B$ and radius $OA$. Both pairs of opposite sides of $AMBO$ are equal, so $AMBO$ is a parallelogram.
